Gen 7 prototype: policy net cloned from Gen 6, and the Gen 6 search reading it

Net (bridge_harness/gen7_net.py, 258,434 parameters): from one seat's view it
predicts the card Gen 6 played and Gen 6's estimated cost of every legal card.
The auction reaches it as the raw calls and as what the hand-fit scorer says
each seat's calls show, routed per suit. Trained on 3,355 deals from the Gen 6
feeds; 61% exact-card agreement on test deals, an equal-best card in its top 3
97% of the time. It should not pick cards; it is a candidate generator.

Player (bridge_harness/gen7.py): Gen6Player plus three switches that read the
net: play-likelihood layout weights from the deal list on, net tie-break, and
unsearched early tricks for fast data tables. Switches off, it plays Gen 6's
game card for card.

Checks (scripts/gen7_check.py) on held-out deals: the local Gen 6 reproduces
the live bot's recorded estimates; play weights add 0.30 nats to the true
layout's log-probability with no measurable change in card quality at tricks
7+; 40-board match +0.30 IMPs/board +- 0.21 (no evidence of a difference).

Nothing here changes Gen 6 or the collectors. See
docs/gen7_prototype_2026-11-11.md.

Gen 7 prototype: net v1 on 5,240 deals, and what lookahead could be worth

Net v1 (828,098 parameters): the same design retrained after adding 2,325
boards from the feeds, including the two v7-capture feeds with gap forks.
On v0's test deals it gives up 0.057 tricks per decision (v0: 0.080) and
plays Gen 6's exact card 65.2% of the time (61.0%).

scripts/gen7_lookahead.py, on 8,809 gap-fork pairs and 500 root tables:
double-dummy cost of Gen 6's card by trick (0.26 at the lead, 0.005 to 0.04
elsewhere), Gen 6's estimated gap against the realized cost of the forced
card (0.47 against 0.39), and how much of double dummy's choice error is
gone after one, two and three tricks of the real play (two tricks: 22% at
the lead, 29% at tricks 3-4, 75% at tricks 7-9).

Results are in docs/gen7_prototype_2026-11-11.md.

Gen 7 prototype: fork tables as training data; lookahead figures are bounds

train_gen7_policy.py --kinds trains on chosen table kinds. Same net, same
5,240 deals, root-table test positions: root tables only 0.068 tricks given
up, with tie forks 0.064, with gap forks 0.065, with both 0.063.

The write-up now says plainly that the lookahead table is an upper bound (the
deeper columns have seen some of the luck play out) and that the fork pairs are
the test bench for a real search.

Gen 7 prototype: tree search and a fork-pair bench to score it

bridge_harness/gen7_tree.py: a few tricks played from each seat's own view
before double dummy. Other seats' cards come from the policy net given what
that seat sees in the layout; the decider's own later card is one choice for
every layout that looks the same to it; DDS at the end of the horizon. With
the horizon at zero it is PIMC exactly (tested).

scripts/gen7_bench.py: rebuilds each gap-fork (and tie-audit) position and
credits an evaluator with what the forked card really gained when it prefers
that card. Gen 6 scores zero by construction.

First results are not in the write-up yet: the two-trick tree as built does
not beat Gen 6 from trick 3 on.

Gen 7 prototype: the tree does not beat Gen 6 from trick 3; sampling noise is not the limit

Tree (bridge_harness/gen7_tree.py): replies from a search from each seat's own view
(reply='search'), the decider's later card from the net or from that search (own='net' |
'search'), counters, and seat_view takes NumPy cards.

Bench (scripts/gen7_bench.py): --to-trick, --splits (held-out deals only), --policy2 with
trees marked net=2 on the same pairs, a fixed file order, each pair's opponent, IMP cost and
place in the net's order, and per_side: the pairs weighted back to one side of one table by
the probability each gap fork was drawn with.

scripts/gen7_noise.py: Gen 6 decisions searched again nine times with fresh layouts, to
measure what sampling noise costs and where the net stands against it.

Write-up: bench results for every tree tried, the weighting to tables and to IMPs a board,
Gen 6's margins on the boards on hand, the noise measurement, the cost of a table by trick,
and the caveat that four in five bench pairs were on deals the net had trained on.

Tests: tests/test_gen7.py TreeTests, 9 pass (2 new).
